primitives.name: Point Cloud Association
primitives.verbatim_quote: According to embodiments of the disclosure, once the plurality of points corresponding to objects 2014 and 2018 have been detected (in step S4008) the method may comprise storing an association between the plurality of points and the location of the at least one object in a storage unit.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'set of 3D points in scene space, dimensionless', 'L': 'location vector of object in image space, meters', 'S': 'storage unit identifier, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Objects are modeled as collections of discrete 3D points; associations are deterministic within frame.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When point detection fails or occlusion occurs, leading to incomplete P.

layer2.mapping: Each point set P maps to a unique object location L via stored association in S; GSI models this as a conditional probability distribution P(L|P).
layer2.telemetry: Association integrity check via cross-frame consistency of P-L pairs.

primitives.name: Spatial Point Processing
primitives.verbatim_quote: Step S4010 comprises processing the plurality of points which have been determined in step S4008.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'input point cloud, dimensionless', 'F': 'processing function, dimensionless', 'O': 'output processed structure, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Processing is context-sensitive but deterministic per embodiment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When F is undefined or non-invertible, O becomes ambiguous.

layer2.mapping: Function F transforms P into O; GSE uses O for pose estimation and motion prediction.
layer2.telemetry: Output structure O validated against biomechanical plausibility constraints.

primitives.name: Temporal Object Tracking
primitives.verbatim_quote: That is, as described above, according to certain embodiments of the disclosure the location of objects in previous images of the scene may be used as a constraint when locating objects in a subsequent image of the scene.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_t': 'object location at time t, meters', 'T': 'temporal transition matrix, dimensionless', 'C': 'constraint function, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Object motion follows predictable dynamics; prior locations constrain current estimates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When T is singular or C is inconsistent, tracking diverges.

layer2.mapping: Temporal sequence {L_t} evolves via T; GSI applies Bayesian update with C to refine L_t+1.
layer2.telemetry: Tracking accuracy measured by deviation from expected trajectory under T.

This forms a foundational mapping from geometric data (P) to semantic identity (L), enabling both static and dynamic object recognition. The processing step (S4010) allows for transformation of raw point sets into structured representations (O), which can include pose models or confidence scores. Temporal coherence is introduced by constraining new object locations based on prior positions, forming a Markovian chain of object states. These primitives enable GSI to perform probabilistic inference over object identities and GSE to reason about transitions in object configurations. Failure modes arise from point detection errors, occlusions, or invalid processing functions, all of which break the isomorphic mappings between P-L and P-O.
